landing.headline: See the outbreak before it spreads.
landing.sub: Report a sick animal in your own language in under two minutes — get instant, explainable triage while district officers watch the live risk map.
landing.disclaimer: Preliminary triage, not a diagnosis — always consult a veterinarian.
landing.feat1b: Reports save on your phone and sync when the signal returns.
landing.feat2b: English, हिंदी and मराठी — farmer-first, voice-friendly.
landing.feat3b: Every AI result shows which symptoms matched and why.

dashboard.heroLine: One report today can protect a whole herd tomorrow.

report.heading: Report
report.lede: Report a sick or dead animal in under two minutes — works offline too.

cases.noVets: No veterinarians are registered in this district.

triage.lede: Rule-based assessment shown transparently — always preliminary, never a diagnosis.
triage.emptyBody: Suspected condition, confidence, reasons, first-aid advisory and next actions. Coming in Part 2.
triage.disclaimer: Preliminary triage, not a diagnosis — always consult a veterinarian.
triage.noCandidates: The signs did not clearly match a known disease — a veterinarian should examine the animal.
triage.emptyNow: Submit a report and its triage result will appear here.

reasons.zoonotic: Can spread to humans — handle with care

triage.matchNote: The reported signs match {matched} of {total} key indicators for this disease.
triage.confNote: Confidence indicates how well the reported signs match this disease.
triage.actionNote: Quick action can prevent spread and protect the herd.
triage.analysisSub: Reasoning, sign match details and other possibilities.
triage.pendingHint: This may take a few seconds.
triage.urgencyNote: Urgency reflects how dangerous the suspected disease is and whether deaths were reported — not only the confidence score.

advisory.care: Provide clean water, shade and soft feed; avoid stress.
advisory.stopSpread: Do not move, sell or share equipment from affected animals.
advisory.zoonotic: This disease can spread to humans — wear gloves, wash hands, and do not consume milk from affected animals.
advisory.notifiable: This is a notifiable disease — inform your local veterinary officer or call the 1962 helpline immediately.
advisory.contactVet: Contact your nearest veterinarian or call the 1962 helpline.
advisory.audioUnavailable: Audio playback is not available here.

whatsapp.heading: WhatsApp & voice reporting
whatsapp.lede: A farmer with no app reports by WhatsApp message — it becomes a real report and lands on your dashboard, with a localised advisory reply sent straight back.
whatsapp.webhookHint: Point the Meta WhatsApp Cloud API at this endpoint. Replies POST to the Graph API when a token is configured; otherwise they're stored and shown in the demo below.
whatsapp.simHint: Type a message exactly as a farmer would (or tap a sample). It flows through the same report → triage → advisory pipeline as the live webhook.
whatsapp.textPlaceholder: e.g. "cattle fever mouth blisters drooling 2 sick 1 dead Shirur"
whatsapp.notParsed: Nothing parsed yet — send a message and the fields appear here.
whatsapp.inboxEmpty: No channel messages yet. Send one in the simulator, or point a real WhatsApp number here.
whatsapp.liveHint: Reports created through this channel appear here and on the Cases & labs dashboard.
whatsapp.webhookNote: For the demo the reply is stored and shown here. Set WHATSAPP_TOKEN and WHATSAPP_PHONE_NUMBER_ID in Vercel to deliver real WhatsApp messages.
whatsapp.poweredBy: Voice notes and translation via Bhashini (optional).
whatsapp.guidanceHint: Turns the number into a button-driven conversation — the best fit for low-literacy farmers. Uses the channel session store (migration 0007).
whatsapp.farmerHeading: Report a sick animal by WhatsApp
whatsapp.farmerLede: No app needed. Message the PashuSetu number with the animal, the signs and the counts — you'll get an instant reply in your own language.
whatsapp.how1: Open WhatsApp and send a message to the number above.
whatsapp.how2: Tell us the animal, the signs and how many are sick or dead.
whatsapp.how3: You'll get the suspected disease and first-aid advice instantly.
whatsapp.exampleSuffix: Tap an example to open WhatsApp with it pre-filled.
whatsapp.yourReportsEmpty: You haven't reported yet. Use the WhatsApp button above, or the Report tab.
whatsapp.exampleReplyTitle: Example of the reply you receive
whatsapp.pilotNote: Save this number — message it in WhatsApp to report a sick animal.
whatsapp.confirmPrefix: Thank you. Your report is recorded.
whatsapp.exampleAdvice: Isolate the affected animal, stop its movement, and contact your nearest vet. First aid: clean the skin, apply soothing ointment, ensure feed and water.
whatsapp.disclaimer: This is preliminary triage, not a diagnosis. Please consult a veterinarian.
whatsapp.tryHint: Tap a sample below or type how the animal looks, then press Send.
whatsapp.realWhatsappSub: Message this number directly from your phone.
whatsapp.realWhatsappNote: For now this is manual — the number goes to PashuSetu. The automatic reply you see above needs the number on Meta's WhatsApp Business API.
whatsapp.simNote: This is an in-app simulation of the WhatsApp flow — it does not send a real WhatsApp message. It runs the same report → triage → reply pipeline a live WhatsApp would.

forecast.title: Tomorrow’s risk outlook
forecast.hint: Report trends, weather and milk-yield signals combined by block.
forecast.noSignals: No unexplained two-day milk dip is active.
forecast.method: Why this is trustworthy: a weekday seasonal median removes normal cycles; heat, humidity and rainfall effects are subtracted before a signal must remain below −2.5σ for two days. This is an early-warning signal, not a diagnosis.

iot.heading: My animal sensors
iot.lede: Connect and monitor sensors fitted to your own animals.
iot.simHint: Demo your three linked collars across healthy days, a heat-wave control and an FMD-like pattern. Real sensors send the same data format.
iot.noDetections: Run the scenario to see explainable detections.
iot.noReports: No sensor report for your herd yet.
iot.disclaimer: Sensor screening is preliminary triage, not a diagnosis. Every automatic report requires veterinary verification and must never replace a veterinarian.
iot.farmerMeaningBody: PashuSetu watches changes in temperature, rumination, activity and milk yield. One unusual reading stays private as an early warning for you—it is not a diagnosis.
iot.privacyNote: Your animal and raw sensor details are private. Other farmers cannot see them. An officer receives only a district-level alert when several matching signals form a serious area pattern; you can always submit a manual report sooner.
